mode.description: Network isolation mode: "open" (unrestricted), "restricted" (internet only, no LAN), or "allowlist" (explicit domain list only)

block_private_networks.description: Block access to RFC 1918 private network ranges

block_metadata_endpoint.description: Block access to cloud instance metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254)

allowed_domains.description: Destinations allowed when mode is "allowlist". Accepts exact hostnames ("api.anthropic.com"), raw IPv4 addresses ("8.8.8.8") and IPv4 CIDRs ("10.0.0.0/8"). Each entry may carry a per-destination port scope as ":ports" — a comma list of single ports and/or lo-hi ranges, e.g. "github.com:443", "192.168.1.50:8080", "10.0.0.0/8:22", "svc:8000-8100" — reachable only on those ports; an entry with no port inherits the global allowed_ports (else all ports). Coi resolves each hostname on the host, installs the addresses in the firewall, and writes the same addresses into the container's /etc/hosts; DNS egress is then blocked, so the container cannot reach an address the firewall was not given. Wildcards are NOT supported and are rejected: with names resolved up front there is no answer to write for a subdomain nobody has asked for yet. List exact hostnames, or the provider's published IP ranges as CIDRs. RFC 1918 ranges are blocked in allowlist mode; reach a single LAN service with a [[network.hosts]] entry and its ports instead.

refresh_interval_minutes.description: How often to re-resolve allowlisted domains and refresh their firewall entries and the container's /etc/hosts (minutes). Set to 0 to disable refreshing, which pins the addresses resolved at startup for the life of the container.

allow_local_network_access.description: Allow established connections from the entire local network, not just the gateway

use_sudo.description: Whether Coi may invoke sudo for network operations (nft/iptables). Defaults to true. Set false to decline passwordless sudo: restricted/allowlist modes then error out (no silent downgrade) and only "open" mode works.

hosts.description: Static name→address entries written into the container's /etc/hosts, with firewall reachability applied to match the active mode. Honored only from trusted-scope config (~/.coi/config.toml or COI_CONFIG); a project ./.coi/config.toml's entries are ignored, since a name→IP mapping is a spoofing primitive and reachability punches a firewall hole. A metadata (169.254.0.0/16) IP is refused. A private IP gets a targeted allow rule in restricted mode, and in allowlist mode too unless allow_local_network_access already opens the LAN; in allowlist mode that rule must be port-scoped (the entry's ports, else allowed_ports) and may not include 53, since allowlist mode blocks all DNS. When allowed_ports is set the host's reachability is scoped to those ports too (allowlist entries inherit the set's port cap; a restricted targeted allow is emitted only for the capped dports), so a host entry cannot reopen the full port range on a LAN box.

dns_servers.description: Pin the DNS resolvers the container may reach on port 53 (restricted mode). Coi accepts :53 only to these IPv4 addresses and rejects every other off-box DNS query, so a compromised container cannot bypass your resolver (e.g. hit 8.8.8.8 directly). The bridge's own resolver is left untouched, so normal resolution keeps working. Honored only from trusted-scope config; not valid in allowlist mode (which blocks all DNS). Only effective alongside a port/allowlist cap, since DNS-over-HTTPS on 443 is otherwise still possible.

allowed_ports.description: Restrict outbound destination ports. In restricted mode this caps the otherwise-open internet egress to just these TCP/UDP ports (ICMP echo still works); in allowlist mode it further constrains the allowlisted hosts. Everything else is rejected. Applies to LAN traffic too: even with allow_local_network_access set, the local network is reachable only on these ports. Bridge-provided DNS is unaffected, so include 53 if the container resolves via an off-box resolver. Honored only from trusted-scope config. Empty/unset keeps the default (all ports).
